tasks.short: Observe the client doing daily tasks at home, ask about difficulties, identify visual impairments affecting life skills, and record the findings.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist observes the client doing self care, home management and meal preparation
Vision rehabilitation therapist asks the client about difficulties with literacy, communication and health management
Vision rehabilitation therapist identifies visual impairments related to basic life skills
Vision rehabilitation therapist records the findings from handwritten notes

tasks.design: Findings are ticked on a tablet checklist per life skill area (self care, literacy, communication, health, home, meals) in the record ({OTHER}) during the visit, with short comments, so they are not typed from notes afterwards. Observing, asking and identifying impairments stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings were written by hand at home visits and typed later.
tasks.still_hard: Clients hide difficulties they are ashamed of.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing the burn marks that show cooking has become unsafe.

reach.learn: Whether life skill problems are known.

evidence.claim: Tablet checklists can fill the record during home visits.

assumptions: Boundary: from the home visit to findings recorded; training is outside.
Input contract: checklist agreed in the team; fallback is handwritten notes.
Observing and identifying do not change.
Ticking the checklist during the visit takes about the time handwritten notes took, so s1 to s3 keep 100. s4 keeps 50 for comments and checking the ticked findings; typing from notes afterwards goes.
research_questions: Are findings in the record on the day of the visit?

incremental.description: Vision rehabilitation therapist keeps the checklist current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: in many homes the tablet is not used during the visit, so findings are still typed from notes and s4 keeps 80 (2.5); high: the checklist is filled during most visits (7.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess which communication devices suit the client, design the instructional program, prepare materials in braille and large print, arrange devices, and note the program.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist assesses which devices such as braillers, keyboards and OCRs suit the client
Vision rehabilitation therapist designs instructional programs to improve communication
Vision rehabilitation therapist prepares lesson materials in braille and large print by hand
Vision rehabilitation therapist prepares the device request: by e-mail today; on the supplier's ordering portal with the client's details filled from the record after the change
Vision rehabilitation therapist checks the final request: the devices match those chosen for the client, the client's details are right, and it goes to the right supplier
Vision rehabilitation therapist submits the checked request to the supplier
Vision rehabilitation therapist notes the program in the record

tasks.design: Lesson texts are written once and converted by braille translation software and large-print templates, so the therapist does not prepare each format by hand. Devices are requested on the supplier's ordering portal with the client's details filled from the record ({OTHER}); the therapist checks and submits each request. Choosing devices and designing the program stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each lesson was prepared separately in braille and large print, and devices requested by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Braille translation software and supplier portals are available.
tasks.still_hard: Braille tables and contractions need checking by a reader.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the device a client will actually use at home.

evidence.claim: Braille translation software converts text into braille for embossing.

assumptions: Boundary: from communication goals to the program noted; training sessions are outside.
Input contract: supplier portal available; fallback is e-mail.
Choosing devices and designing programs stay with the therapist.

s3 keeps 60 because the lesson text is still written by the therapist; converting it to each format goes. s4 keeps 55 for choosing items and supplier questions; the check (s4b) and submission (s4c) take 1 each. s5 is a first record and keeps its full time.
research_questions: Do devices arrive before the program starts more often?

incremental.description: Vision rehabilitation therapist checks converted braille.

approvals.approved_version: The device request with devices and client details exactly as checked by the therapist in s4b, submitted once to the named supplier; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: conversions need many corrections, so s3 keeps 80, and few suppliers have a portal, so s4 keeps 85 (5.9); high: conversion and portals as designed (14.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train clients to use adaptive equipment such as large print, lamps, software and electronic devices, set up devices, make home practice instructions, and note progress.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist trains clients to use adaptive equipment
Vision rehabilitation therapist sets up devices and software for the client
Vision rehabilitation therapist writes home practice instructions for each device
Vision rehabilitation therapist notes training progress

tasks.design: Home practice instructions come from a shared library of large-print and audio instructions per device ({DOCS}) that the therapist adapts, instead of writing new ones. Progress is ticked per device skill in the record ({OTHER}); this first record keeps most of its time. Training clients and setting up devices stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions were written per client and progress kept in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared instruction libraries and record templates are easy to keep.
tasks.still_hard: Device software updates change the steps.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the lamp position that lets a client read again.

reach.learn: Whether they keep using the equipment.

evidence.claim: Shared instruction libraries in large print and audio can be kept per device.

assumptions: Boundary: from equipment chosen to progress noted; supply is outside.
Input contract: library kept by the team; fallback is writing per client.
Training and setup do not change.
s3 keeps 50 for adapting each library text to the client. s4 keeps 85: ticking skills saves some typing, but the progress note is the therapist's own record.
research_questions: Do clients keep using equipment after three months?

incremental.description: Vision rehabilitation therapist updates instructions after device updates.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the library covers few of the devices clients use, so s3 keeps 80 (1.2); high: the library covers most devices (2.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find literature and courses, read literature, attend courses and conferences, collaborate with colleagues, and keep a log of development activities.

steps.what: Vision rehabilitation therapist searches for relevant literature and courses
Vision rehabilitation therapist reads literature
Vision rehabilitation therapist attends continuing education and conferences
Vision rehabilitation therapist collaborates with colleagues in peer meetings
Course providers register the therapist's attendance in the professional register's portfolio
Vision rehabilitation therapist keeps a log of professional development activities in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Journal alerts and the professional register's course list send new articles and accredited courses on vision rehabilitation, so the therapist does not search. Course providers register attendance in the register's portfolio, which replaces the personal spreadsheet. Reading, attending and peer meetings stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources were searched by hand and activities logged in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Journals send alerts; professional registers take points from providers.
tasks.human_edge: Learning from a colleague's hard case.

evidence.claim: Journals send content alerts and professional registers can take attendance points from providers.

assumptions: Boundary: from development needs to activities logged; re-registration is outside.
Input contract: providers register points; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Reading and attending do not change.
Colleagues' time does not change. Providers' registration (s4b, share 1) is outside the therapist's savings. s5 keeps 30 for adding activities providers do not register and checking the portfolio.
research_questions: Is the portfolio complete at re-registration?

incremental.description: Vision rehabilitation therapist adds activities providers did not register.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many providers do not register attendance, so s5 keeps 60, and alerts miss relevant sources, so s1 keeps 80 (6.1); high: providers register and alerts work as designed (13.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The vision rehabilitation therapist keeps observing, designing programs, training clients and learning; typed notes, hand-made braille materials and spreadsheet logs shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist with more time with clients.

job.title: Low Vision Therapists, Orientation and Mobility Specialists, and Vision Rehabilitation Therapists
